title: A live GraphCast run may have forecast Hurricane Lee's landfall in Nova Scotia about nine days ahead
summary: DeepMind says that a live GraphCast run predicted about nine days in advance that Hurricane Lee would make landfall in Nova Scotia; no source documents a forecaster using the run.
account: The editorial of Newsletter 177 (Autumn 2023) of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) confirms that GraphCast, Pangu-Weather and FourCastNet were made available on ECMWF's public charts pages from ECMWF's own initial conditions. Google DeepMind's blog post of 14 November 2023 states that in September 2023 a live version of its publicly available GraphCast model, deployed on the ECMWF website, predicted about nine days in advance that Hurricane Lee would make landfall in Nova Scotia. DeepMind dates the forecast only as “September”. Lee, by then post-tropical, made landfall on Long Island in southwestern Nova Scotia around 2000 UTC on 16 September 2023. Its maximum sustained winds were about 55 knots. On 14 November 2023 MIT Technology Review relayed the nine-day claim from Rémi Lam, a staff research scientist at DeepMind. It added that traditional forecasting models pinpointed Nova Scotia only six days in advance. The article quotes no ECMWF staff on Lee. The tropical cyclone report on Lee by the National Hurricane Center (NHC), dated 21 March 2024, records the landfall and mentions no AI model. It reports that official NHC track errors were exceptionally low through 72 hours and below five-year means through 120 hours. The NHC verification report for 2023 contains no entry for an AI model, and no ECMWF document recording the Lee forecast is on record. A preprint by researchers at the Cooperative Institute for Research in the Atmosphere (CIRA) at Colorado State University, who are independent of DeepMind, mentions Lee only for its intensity and structure. In October 2025 researchers at CIRA published a verification of AI weather models for the 2023 cyclone season, run from initial conditions of the Global Forecast System. They found that GraphCast had the lowest mean track errors from 96 hours onward, by up to 13% against the ECMWF model, although the differences were not statistically significant. They do not report a track result for Lee. No cited source documents a forecaster or authority acting on the GraphCast Lee run.
purpose: Global medium-range weather forecasting by machine learning, up to 10 days ahead at a resolution of 0.25 degree, including the prediction of severe events such as tropical cyclone tracks. This forecast served that purpose.

display.answer: The nine-day Lee claim comes from DeepMind's blog post, and MIT Technology Review relayed it from a DeepMind scientist. The National Hurricane Center report and the ECMWF editorial confirm the landfall and the experimental availability separately. The CIRA verification of October 2025 is independent of DeepMind and reports no track result for Lee.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: DeepMind says that a live GraphCast run predicted about nine days in advance that Hurricane Lee would make landfall in Nova Scotia; no source documents a forecaster using the run.
fields.account: The editorial of Newsletter 177 (Autumn 2023) of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) confirms that GraphCast, Pangu-Weather and FourCastNet were made available on ECMWF's public charts pages from ECMWF's own initial conditions. Google DeepMind's blog post of 14 November 2023 states that in September 2023 a live version of its publicly available GraphCast model, deployed on the ECMWF website, predicted about nine days in advance that Hurricane Lee would make landfall in Nova Scotia. DeepMind dates the forecast only as “September”. Lee, by then post-tropical, made landfall on Long Island in southwestern Nova Scotia around 2000 UTC on 16 September 2023. Its maximum sustained winds were about 55 knots. On 14 November 2023 MIT Technology Review relayed the nine-day claim from Rémi Lam, a staff research scientist at DeepMind. It added that traditional forecasting models pinpointed Nova Scotia only six days in advance. The article quotes no ECMWF staff on Lee. The tropical cyclone report on Lee by the National Hurricane Center (NHC), dated 21 March 2024, records the landfall and mentions no AI model. It reports that official NHC track errors were exceptionally low through 72 hours and below five-year means through 120 hours. The NHC verification report for 2023 contains no entry for an AI model, and no ECMWF document recording the Lee forecast is on record. A preprint by researchers at the Cooperative Institute for Research in the Atmosphere (CIRA) at Colorado State University, who are independent of DeepMind, mentions Lee only for its intensity and structure. In October 2025 researchers at CIRA published a verification of AI weather models for the 2023 cyclone season, run from initial conditions of the Global Forecast System. They found that GraphCast had the lowest mean track errors from 96 hours onward, by up to 13% against the ECMWF model, although the differences were not statistically significant. They do not report a track result for Lee. No cited source documents a forecaster or authority acting on the GraphCast Lee run.
